rationale: As a portfolio, the sheet does not pass. Although 14 options are shown, only about 9 are materially legible as different mass families, and a dominant compact box/prism/notch lineage occupies roughly 43% of the set. The set over-relies on repeated footprints and roof/upper-profile changes, so it reads as one family with cosmetic edits rather than a broad search. The strongest program-fit moves are the split-threshold bar, the cross-mass puncture, and the embedded void cases, because they better express an active street edge plus one usable public void. The portfolio still lacks enough true family separation in courtyard, split-wing, lifted, and bridged relations to satisfy the contract for a passing 20-option neighborhood-living massing set.

repeated_family_groups.shared_language: one-box profiled prism/block/slab variants with a single main body and only shallow roof/profile differences; same compact street-box family repeated across the set
entry-notch / stepped or bent-bar upper profile over a similar compact base, producing near-duplicate section logic
voided block / open-court variant with repeated orthogonal footprint and similar roof termination

required_next_relations: Need at least one genuinely different courtyard family with a more explicit carved-through public void, not just a shallow notch.
Need one split-wing or crossed-mass option where the ground threshold is spatially split, not merely clipped.
Need one lifted-volume composition that produces a real active ground edge under the mass, preserving a calm upper block.
Need one bent-bar or bridged composition that makes the west access side read as a true public threshold.
Need one terrace-to-court sequence where the public void is usable and not only a roof step.
Need at least ten materially legible families overall; the current set over-concentrates on compact box/prism and notched variants.
Avoid producing more variants by only changing roof chamfer, minor curvature, or notch depth; change the primary volumetric relation instead.
